title: Establishing translational neuroimaging tools for quantitative assessment of energy metabolism and metabolic reprogramming in healthy and diseased human brain at 7T
text:
The next generation high-resolution high-performance neurometabolic imaging techniques as established in
this project will enable quantitative and whole-brain imaging of key metabolic rates and other important
neurophysiological parameters associated with major energy metabolism pathways in healthy and diseased
human brain on an FDA-approved 7 Tesla clinical MRI scanner. The success of this project will provide
translatable neuroimaging tools that can be applied in a wide range of biomedical, neuroscience and clinical
research for assessing human brain energetic status and its changes. New insights from these areas of
research are invaluable for understanding the energetic mechanisms of neurological disorders and ultimately
improving our ability to diagnose, monitor progression, and assess the effects of treatments for brain diseases.

title: Dissecting ventral pallidal plasticity in punishment-resistant opioid self-administration
text:
Misuse of prescription opioids is a significant public health and economic burden; in 2020 in the United States,
more than 9.9 million people reported prescription opioid misuse, and prescription opioids contributed to over
17,000 overdose deaths. A defining symptom of opioid use disorder is the inability to abstain from drug
consumption in the face of aversive life consequences, which afflicts only a subset of individuals who take
prescription opioids. Understanding the neural circuits that distinguish this subset of individuals who cannot
inhibit drug consumption is necessary to predict which patients are at risk for developing opioid use disorder,
and to prevent or reverse these neural circuit changes as a potential therapy.

title: Emory University Lung Cancer SPORE
text:
OVERALL NARRATIVE
Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths, with more than 1.8 million deaths/year globally.
We plan to conduct translational and innovative research to define how stem-like CD8 T cells interact with
myeloid cells with focus on new inhibitory surface molecules identified by our group and evaluate a novel first-
in-class IL-2R / biased partial agonist (STK-012) to generate more potent effector CD8T cells against NSCLC;
to develop and validate a multimodal AI-based model to predict outcomes for patients with stage III NSCLC
leveraging a recently completed phase III clinical trial by ECOG-ACRIN; and to develop a novel strategy of
targeting a noncanonical mitochondrial metabolic pathway to treat lung cancer. The Emory Lung Cancer SPORE
program brings together an outstanding and multidisciplinary team of oncologists, immunologists, computational
scientists, drug discovery experts, and translational researchers to address critical questions that will improve
the outcome for patients with this lethal disease.

title: Core C - High Spatial and Temporal Resolution Imaging Core
text:
We propose to expand the services offered by the High Spatial and Temporal Resolution Imaging (HSTRI) Core
established during Phase I COBRE with the goal of providing instrumentation and scientific expertise that will
enable COBRE Project Leaders to perform crucial experiments that are not possible in their individual
laboratories. With the assistance of expert staff and unrestricted access to these instruments, we expect the
HSTRI Core to greatly enhance the competitiveness of Project Leaders in future grant applications and promote
their recognition and contribution to their respective field at the international level, both of which will accelerate
the pace of discovery. This facility is specifically designed to meet the needs of our Project Leaders but will also
enhance the overall capacity for research by serving as a campus wide infrastructure to assist researchers at
the University of Nevada, Reno, and the UNR School of Medicine.

title: Towards screening with high-resolution, low-dose, dedicated breast CT
text:
Dedicated breast CT is a new imaging technique that does not require breast compression, provides fully 3D
images, and can eliminate tissue superposition which could reduce unnecessary call-backs for additional
imaging and could reduce missed cancers. Building on our prior work on the hardware design and engineering
of the breast CT system, in this research, we focus on image reconstruction in breast CT to determine the optimal
method, followed by a comparative study with digital breast tomosynthesis (also referred to as 3D
mammography) to determine the benefits of dedicated breast CT for translating it to breast cancer screening.

title: The molecular and structural basis of glycoRNA-receptor interaction
text:
This project investigates the molecular principles by which neutrophil glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) interact
with endothelial P-selectin to mediate neutrophil recruitment. By defining the chemical, biochemical, and
structural basis of glycoRNA–receptor recognition, this research will reveal fundamental mechanisms by which
extracellular glycoRNAs act as ligands for adhesion receptors.

title: Personalizing genetic test results management and outcomes after diagnosis of cancer: the Georgia-California SEER Genelink Study
text:
The growing use of genetic testing across adult cancer diagnoses is driving the
development of precision oncology: a new paradigm for personalizing cancer treatment and prevention based
on genetic testing results. We pioneered the Georgia-California Genetic Testing Linkage Initiative, which linked
industry-provided germline genetic testing data to Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results program cancer
registry records, and are now markedly expanding the initiative to include all adults diagnosed with cancer in
Georgia and California from 2013-23 and genetic testing results through 2025. We will use this unique data
infrastructure to determine whether the management of genetic testing results is effectively personalized to
patient clinical factors and whether cancer mortality varies by genetic testing results, across cancer types.

title: Molecular determinants of condensate assembly in heterogeneous environments
text:
Biomolecular condensates are intracellular structures that organize cellular components into “membraneless
organelles,” which play essential roles in a wide range of biological processes including gene transcription, protein
translation, and cell signaling. This research program will determine the biochemical features of protein/RNA
molecules that govern the molecular compositions and assembly mechanisms of biomolecular condensates,
allowing us to connect changes in protein/RNA sequences to changes in membraneless compartmentalization
within the complex intracellular environment. By leveraging modern simulation and machine-learning methods,
our work will (1) provide vital insights into the mechanisms that cells use to control condensate assembly and
composition, (2) introduce sequence design tools for engineering protein/RNA molecules to regulate condensate
assembly and composition, and (3) lay the groundwork for future therapeutic strategies based on manipulating
this form of intracellular spatial organization.

title: Influence of neuromelanin on single dopaminergic neurons in Parkinson's disease.
text:
Disease-modifying treatments for Parkinson’s disease do not currently exist, possibly due to weaknesses in the
rodent models typically used for preclinical studies. This project will leverage a novel mouse model of
neuromelanin accumulation in dopaminergic neurons to overcome a key difference between human and rodent
brains that could contribute to disease pathogenesis. Results will provide a wealth of information in susceptible
cell populations with direct relevance to Parkinson’s pathology, informing the design of future experiments into
novel therapeutic targets.

title: HPV genomic structure in cervical cancer radiation response and recurrence detection
text:
Cervical cancer patients treated with standard of care (SOC) chemoradiation therapy (CRT) commonly
experience disease recurrence, and current clinical testing and cancer genomic data cannot predict which
patients will fail therapy before treatment or promptly detect disease recurrence after treatment. Our recent
publications demonstrated that HPV genotypes and HPV alternative splicing affect LACC CRT response and
patient outcome, and our preliminary data additionally identified a diversity of predictive HPV genomic structures
(HPV-GS), including HPV-human gene fusions which affect their human oncogene partner expression. In this
proposal, we will develop new HPV-GS based pre-treatment biomarkers, identify CRT-resistant HPV-GS in the
context of CRT-induced clonal evolution, examine their mechanistic significance, and evaluate whether HPV-GS
ctDNA tests can monitor LACC recurrence and metastasis.

title: Regulation of Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity by cGMP-mRNA Crosstalk in Mouse Models of Alzheimer's Disease and Aging
text:
Alzheimer's disease is a growing public health crisis with limited treatment options. This project explores an
innovative mechanism by which cyclic GMP (cGMP) directly binds claudin-5 mRNA to enhance blood-brain
barrier integrity. Understanding this RNA-based regulation could lead to new therapeutic strategies that target
cerebrovascular dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease, potentially delaying or modifying disease progression.

title: Identification and assessment of unconventional tumor-associated antigens as potential targets for cytotoxic T-cell based immunotherapy of cancer
text:
Immunotherapy for the treatment of cancer relies on the activity of specialized white blood cells called
cytotoxic (or “killer”) T cells which are capable of eliminating tumors, provided they recognize specific
targets on the tumor cell surface. Identifying these tumor-specific targets in cancer patients will allow for
the design and administration of personalized immunotherapies with the potential to benefit or even cure
these patients. The major goal of this grant proposal is to use specialize methodologies to identify novel
and unconventional immunotherapeutic targets for melanoma, thus enabling the development of
effective immunotherapeutic treatments for patients with these and other cancer types.

title: Molecular and Chemical Regulation of Cell Death in Disease
text:
Apoptosis and necroptosis are essential pathways of cell death with distinct biochemical mechanisms that play essential
roles in development and disease. Therefore, understanding their regulations is vital for improving human health. The
outcomes of our studies will provide innovative molecular insights and uncover potential drug candidates, paving the way
for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for human diseases linked to cell death dysregulation.

title: Advancing cryo-EM technology to address difficult biological questions
text:
This application proposes to advance single particle cryo-EM technology so that challenging biological questions
beyond atomic structure determinations, particularly protein dynamics and conformational transitions between
conformational states, can be studied.

title: Integrative Single-Cell Analysis of Aging-Associated Changes in Human Hematopoietic Stem Cell Heterogeneity
text:
This research is relevant to public health because understanding the molecular drivers of hematopoietic
stem cell aging and age-associated immune dysfunction may inform strategies to mitigate diseases such
as hematological disorders and cardiovascular disease. It aligns with the NIH’s mission to advance
fundamental knowledge that enhances health and extends lifespan.

title: Optoelectroactive citrate biocomposites for bone regeneration
text:
Existing bone regenerative biomaterials are featured with inabilities to mimic the native tissue composition, and
slow bone regeneration among others. In this proposal, we will reach a fundamental understanding of
unprecedented synergistic optoelectro-metabonegenic regulation mechanism in bone repair, will design
biomimetic optoelectroactive citrate biocomposites to achieve promoted bone repair. Our study will hold the
potential to transform the fields of issue engineering and regeneration, and bioelectronics among others.

title: Next Generation Sequencing Shared Resource
text: NEXT GENERATION SEQUENCING SHARED RESOURCE (NGS-SR): ABSTRACT The Next Generation Sequencing Shared Resource (NGS-SR) provides the University of Florida Health Cancer Center (UFHCC) members with access to centralized, state-of-the-art, cost-effective next generation sequencing services to advance cancer research. The NGS-SR is an institutionally-managed shared resource supported by UFHCC through a partnership with the UF Interdisciplinary Center for Biotechnology Research, a campus-wide shared biotechnology resource. Located within the Cancer & Genetics Research Complex providing convenient access for UFHCC members, NGS-SR includes 4 staff members under the supervision of Moraga, who has over 30 years of experience in DNA sequencing technologies. During the recent COVID-19 pandemic, the NGS-SR was identified as an essential campus resource and remained staffed and open to the UF research community. NGS-SR service requests and invoicing are managed via the CrossLab laboratory management system. Key sequencing technologies available include instruments from Illumina (NovaSeq6000, MiSeq), PacBio SEQUEL IIe, Oxford Nanopore PromethION, and the 10x Genomics Chromium single-cell RNA-Seq and VISIUM spatial transcriptomics platforms. Raw sequencing read data are directly transferred to the HiPerGator high- performance computing cluster for downstream bioinformatics analysis. UFHCC investments in instrumentation include the Illumina NovaSeq6000, PacBio SEQUEL IIe, mosquito® liquid handling robot, and 10x Genomics Chromium single cell platform. The NGS-SR works in collaboration with the UFHCC Biostatistics and Quantitative Sciences Shared Resource to provide no cost consultation in effective experimental design and best practices in computational analysis of large-scale multi-omic data sets. NGS-SR supports studies in DNA structural and gene variant analysis, microbiome and metagenome analysis, bulk and single cell ATAC-Seq and RNA-Seq, ChIP-Seq, and whole genome sequencing. Since 2016, 54 unique members have used NGS-SR, of which 45 have peer-reviewed funding. There has been an increase in the number of members using NGS-SR each year and an increase in sequencing runs, supporting 54 peer-reviewed publications, with 24% having IF >10. Mechanisms of Oncogenesis and the Cancer Therapeutics and Host Response members represent major users. The effectiveness of the NGS-SR in meeting member needs is assessed by annual surveys, feedback from the NGS-SR Scientific Advisory Group, and recommendations from the Shared Resources Oversight Committee. In response to user requests for lower costs, the acquisition of the NovaSeq6000 reduced sequencing costs by 50% and the use of robotics has reduced RNA-Seq library prep costs by 75%. In alignment with the UFHCC Strategic Plan, Momentum 2027, the demand for NGS-SR services is anticipated to grow with recruitments in molecular epidemiology, immunobiology, and RNA epigenetics. In response, NGS-SR will continue to lower costs through increased automation, expand services including spatial transcriptomics, and adopt new technologies to increase capabilities in cost effective single cell transcriptomics.

title: Predicting acute and dynamic suicide risk in rural sexual minorities
text:
Rigorous research is needed to identify mechanisms contributing to sexual minority health disparities,
particularly from an intersectionality perspective. The intersectionality of geographic location and sexual
orientation can profoundly impact prevalence of suicidal thoughts and behaviors, as rural sexual minorities
experience disproportionate burden of suicidal thoughts and behaviors, often reside in high-stigma
environments, and have limited access to healthcare resources. This project uses an innovative mixed
methods approach to clarify acute and dynamic mechanisms underlying suicidal thoughts and behavior
disparities among rural sexual minority adults and will inform therapeutic targets for suicide prevention in this
uniquely high-risk population.

title: Biostatistics & Database Core
text: PROJECT SUMMARY – Biostatistics & Database Core (CL: Xie) The Biostatistics & Database Core is an integral part of this program project grant (PPG) renewal “From Molecules to Complex Syndromes: Using Networks to Understand Heterogeneity in FTD-TDP and Aging” at the University of Pennsylvania (Penn) Perelman School of Medicine (PSOM). The goal of our Core is to support the data management, database, multimodal data integration through harmonized workflows, data sharing to consortia and external collaborators, statistics, bioinformatics, and related computational needs of the PPG investigators to address our innovative overall hypothesis that FTLD-TDP is complex disorder that requires a wholistic nanoscale-to-exposome approach to unravel novel biomarkers and mechanisms at the cellular, mesoscopic, macroscopic, and systems network levels to breakdown barriers to therapeutic success. The services provided by our Core include: (a) support for multimodal data form/questionnaire design and development, database development and management, data entry, database audit trail, database security, database backup, and stringent data quality control procedures, (b) computing and programming support for all PPG activities, including implementation and integration of hardware and software upgrades necessary for data management and research, routine and archival off-site backup of computing systems central to the PPG, (c) biostatistical support for all study aspects of Projects and Cores from inception to publication, including development of study design, performing sample size and power calculations, and performing analyses of the PPG data, (d) support multimodal data integration analyses across Cores and Projects, (e) provide oversight in the dissemination of data in adherence with data management & sharing plan, and (f) development of new statistical methodologies and extension of existing methodologies where needed for analyses of the PPG data. Thus, the Biostatistics & Database Core plays an important and significant role that is critical to the progress of research and the conduct of studies in the PPG.

title: Defining and exploiting therapeutically the role of the neuropeptide receptor PAC1 in tumor-infiltrating pericytes that drives melanoma progression.
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health as it focuses on the discovery of a novel neuron-pericyte
interaction involved in the entangled relationship between the nervous system and melanoma. The goal of this
study is to determine the mechanisms by which the neuropeptide receptor PAC1 regulates melanoma
development and metastases and the relevance of PAC1 expression in the outcomes of patients with melanoma.
We will use human melanoma specimens and clinically relevant melanoma mouse models in combination with
genetic state-of-the-art technologies to reveal novel pathways for the mechanistic and therapeutic significance
of PACAP-PAC1 signaling role in melanoma progression.
